_fixture: Synthetic example for UI development; not real data. Tables only, so indicators is empty; fetch the tables by run id.

algorithm.description: ADF and KPSS tests on the imbalance price, its half-hourly change and its daily change; the differences AutoARIMA would apply; and the price's AR spectrum.

tables.sample: The gap-free stretch tested: its first and last period, its length and how many periods of the range were left out
tables.unit_root: ADF (null: unit root) and KPSS (null: stationary) per series and deterministic term: statistic, critical values at 1%, 2.5% (KPSS only), 5% and 10%, the levels at which the null is rejected, lags and observations
tables.difference_orders: Seasonal and regular differences (0 or 1) AutoARIMA would apply, with the seasonal difference tested and with it fixed at 1
tables.spectrum: AR spectral density in (GBP/MWh)^2 per cycle per half-hour, by frequency in cycles per half-hour, with the matching period in hours
tables.spectrum_fit: The Burg AR order and innovation variance behind the spectrum, or why it could not be computed

param_descriptions.season_length: Seasonal period in half-hours for the seasonal difference and its test (48 = daily)
param_descriptions.adf_lags: Lagged differences in each ADF regression (48 = one day); fixed, not selected
param_descriptions.kpss_lags: Autocovariances in KPSS's long-run variance; at least 48 for half-hourly data, or the test rejects stationarity too often
param_descriptions.regressions: Deterministic terms tested: c (constant) and/or ct (constant and linear trend)
param_descriptions.spectrum_order: AR order of the Burg fit; 48 can resolve every harmonic of the daily cycle
param_descriptions.nfft: Frequency grid size; a multiple of 336 puts daily and weekly harmonics on it
param_descriptions.max_periods: Most recent gap-free periods tested (2688 = 56 days)

algorithm.limitations: Retrospective: statistics of the whole stretch, with no pass/fail verdict. There are no p-values, only the tabulated levels at which each null is rejected; the tests assume a constant variance, which imbalance prices do not have. ADF and KPSS have opposite nulls, so read them together. difference_orders uses Orchid's default KPSS lags, which can over-difference persistent series, while 48 KPSS lags make it slow to reject on a few weeks of data. The spectrum is of an AR model fitted to the price, not a raw periodogram.
